directAnswer: You can mirror your Android device to a TV using built-in casting features like Google Cast or by connecting via HDMI with an adapter.
summary: Mirroring your Android device to a TV can enhance your viewing experience by allowing you to display content on a larger screen. Here are the methods you can use to achieve this.

sections.heading: Using Google Cast
sections.body: Most modern TVs support Google Cast. Ensure your TV and Android device are connected to the same Wi-Fi network, then use the Cast feature in your device's Quick Settings.

sections.heading: Using HDMI Connection
sections.body: If your TV does not support wireless casting, you can connect your Android device directly to the TV using an HDMI adapter compatible with your device.

steps.title: Enable Screen Mirroring
steps.detail: Swipe down from the top of your Android screen to access Quick Settings and tap on 'Cast' or 'Screen Mirroring'.

steps.title: Select Your TV
steps.detail: From the list of available devices, select your TV. If prompted, confirm the connection on your TV.

steps.title: Adjust Display Settings
steps.detail: You may need to adjust display settings on your TV or Android device for optimal viewing.

steps.title: Using HDMI Adapter
steps.detail: Connect your Android device to the TV using an HDMI adapter, then switch the TV input to the corresponding HDMI port.

faqs.question: What if my TV doesn't support casting?
faqs.answer: You can use an HDMI adapter to connect your Android device directly to the TV.

faqs.question: Will screen mirroring drain my battery?
faqs.answer: Yes, screen mirroring can consume more battery power, so it's advisable to keep your device plugged in during use.

faqs.question: Can I mirror my Android device to multiple TVs?
faqs.answer: Most Android devices allow you to connect to one TV at a time for mirroring.

caveats: Some older Android devices may not support screen mirroring features.
